title: Omitting the password element leaves the verifier in its default 'no verification option' state, and that switch case returns success
index_line: T-0078 · AUTH_DECISION · WS-Security token without a Password element: parser default SendNone reaches the verifier's default branch · dotnet · corroborated
invariant_violated: The verifier assumed every token would name a password option; when the element is absent the option keeps its constructor default (SendNone) and the verification switch's default branch returns without comparing anything — so 'no credential supplied' was executed as 'no credential required'.

mechanism.does: a SOAP request carries a UsernameToken with a Username but no <wsse:Password> element at all
UsernameToken.LoadXml never sets _passwordOption because there is no Password node, leaving the default SendNone
VerifyPassword switches on the option; SendNone falls to the default branch, which returns without any comparison
the token is accepted because verification was skipped, not because a credential matched
the caller marks the token authenticated and attaches the resulting identity
the SOAP body's stagingTaskData is deserialized with SoapFormatter as the configured staging user

source.http.body.value: a SOAP envelope whose UsernameToken omits the Password element entirely

guard.signature.value: the password-verification routine that returns success on its SendNone default branch

sink.deser.native.value: stagingTaskData deserialized by SoapFormatter once the token is accepted

guard.pipeline.value: the XML-security pipeline that decides the password option from the message itself instead of from policy

preconditions.expr: the staging SOAP endpoint answers unauthenticated
the deployment uses the WSE3 UsernameTokenManager path with user-name/password staging authentication
a token with no Password element is accepted where one with a wrong password is rejected

success: a Password-less UsernameToken returns a staging-processing result instead of a security fault
the response differs from the same request carrying a wrong Password element
failure_like: the library rejects tokens without a password ('must contain password')
the service is configured for X.509 authentication
false_positive: a fault about a missing username token means the token was parsed but the user did not resolve — not this bug
a 200 from the .asmx page itself is the WSDL/landing page, not authentication success

hazards: message-driven verification options are a recurring pattern: the attacker chooses the policy by choosing the message shape
any 'if no credential present, skip the check' branch in an auth library
default enum members in security switches are the concrete tell
non_transfers: verifiers that require a password element as a schema-validated mandatory field
policy that fixes the password option server-side

evidence.target: Kentico Xperience <= 13.0.178, Staging Sync Server with the 'None' password type (CVE-2025-2747)

provenance.author: watchTowr Labs
provenance.corroborates: CVE-2025-2747: UsernameToken.LoadXml leaves _passwordOption at its default PasswordOption.SendNone when no <wsse:Password> element is present; VerifyPassword switches on that option and the default branch returns without comparing anything, so a password-less token authenticates
